title: Exploring Students’ Multimodal Representations of Ideas About Epistemic Reading of Scientific Texts in Generative AI Tools
venue: Journal of Science Education and Technology
extended_summary:
This paper examines how students represent their ideas about reading scientific texts generated by generative AI tools, a process the authors call GenAI-science epistemic reading. The problem addressed is that students need to draw on both their understanding of science and their understanding of GenAI in order to critically interpret AI-generated scientific information, yet existing measures in this area are often limited to Likert-scale surveys. The study asks what students’ multimodal representations of these ideas look like in terms of presentational, organisational, and orientational meanings.

The study uses a qualitative collective case study approach and develops a multimodal instrument in which students draw and write short explanations about (1) how ChatGPT/Poe generates scientific texts and (2) how they themselves read scientific texts in these tools. The authors analyze 44 students’ drawings and written responses using Lemke’s framework of presentational, organisational, and orientational meaning, and from these data they construct an analytical framework with categories such as epistemic trust, epistemic knowledge, organisational form, and representations of the nature of science and GenAI. Although the responses were collected before an explicit-reflective instructional activity that was part of a larger project, this paper focuses on the pre-instruction representations rather than testing intervention effects.

Participants were 44 Grade 8 and Grade 9 students in Hong Kong participating in extracurricular lessons. The instructional context involved a bilingual teacher who had prior online training workshops on implementing the teaching approach. Students completed the multimodal task in two classrooms before instruction, and the broader project centered on improving students’ understanding of epistemic reading of scientific texts from sources including GenAI and online media.

The main conclusion is that a multimodal approach is useful for characterising students’ ideas about GenAI-science epistemic reading in ways that standard survey instruments may miss. Students expressed a range of epistemic trust positions, including trust, critical thinking, confusion, and non-evaluation, and used different semiotic modes to express these ideas. The paper’s core contribution is an analytical framework teachers and researchers can use to diagnose and discuss students’ epistemic understanding of AI-generated scientific texts. The authors argue that such multimodal representations can serve as a richer diagnostic and instructional tool for future intervention studies on GenAI in science education.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: An OpenAI generative AI chatbot based on large language models that generates text responses to user prompts.
identified_tools.use_case: Used as the focal GenAI tool in prompts asking Grade 8–9 students to draw and write how ChatGPT generates science texts and how they read scientific texts in ChatGPT; the study examined students’ multimodal representations about GenAI-science epistemic reading rather than ChatGPT performance or learning effects.

findings.finding_summary: In a qualitative classroom-based case study of 44 eighth- and ninth-grade students, most students did not express an epistemic-trust stance toward scientific information in ChatGPT in either prompt (54.5% for Q1 on how ChatGPT/Poe generated scientific texts; 43.5% for Q2 on how they read scientific texts in ChatGPT/Poe). Some students expressed trust in ChatGPT’s science outputs (22.7% for Q1; 11.4% for Q2, written mode), while others expressed confusion or critical thinking, indicating varied epistemic reasoning rather than a uniform stance.
findings.measure: Students’ multimodal representations of epistemic trust and epistemic knowledge about reading scientific texts in ChatGPT/Poe, coded from drawings and writing

findings.finding_summary: Students more often represented implicit nature of science than explicit nature of science when depicting ChatGPT/Poe and scientific texts: 81.8% of drawn/written responses in Q1 and 61.4% in Q2 were coded as implicit nature of science. By contrast, more students represented explicit nature of GenAI in both drawn and written modes (52.3% in Q1; 36.4% in Q2), suggesting stronger articulation of how GenAI works than of how science knowledge is produced.
findings.measure: Orientational meaning codes for explicit/implicit nature of science and nature of GenAI in student multimodal responses

findings.finding_summary: For epistemic knowledge, students commonly represented ChatGPT/Poe as either simple conversation or search-like functionality. In Q1, 31.8% represented simple conversation and 22.7% represented Google search; in Q2, 25.0% represented simple conversation in writing and 18.2% represented general function in writing, showing partial but often simplified conceptions of how the tool generates science text.
findings.measure: Presentational meaning codes for epistemic knowledge (e.g., simple conversation, Google search, general function, large language model) in drawings/writing

identified_tools.name: POE
identified_tools.description: A named generative AI chatbot platform used to generate text responses to user prompts.
identified_tools.use_case: Used alongside ChatGPT in the study prompts as an example GenAI tool for students to represent how the tool generates science texts and how they read scientific texts produced by it.

findings.finding_summary: Across the combined ChatGPT/Poe prompts, students showed heterogeneous epistemic ideas about GenAI-produced scientific texts, with many giving no explicit evaluation of trustworthiness and others expressing trust, confusion, or critical thinking. The study’s central result was methodological: multimodal drawing-plus-writing elicited diverse representations of students’ epistemic reading ideas about ChatGPT/Poe that would be difficult to capture with Likert-scale measures alone.
findings.measure: Qualitative coding of students’ multimodal representations about GenAI-science epistemic reading in ChatGPT/Poe

quality_tier_rationale: This is an empirical qualitative collective case study with n=44 students and systematic coding, but it is not an RCT/QED and does not test causal effects of a tool on learning outcomes. Evidence is therefore exploratory and descriptive.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper does not report effect sizes or outcome gains from using ChatGPT/POE; findings concern students’ representations and an analytical framework. Impact on student outcomes is therefore unclear.
